title: Psalm 80 (Septuagint) = Psalm 81 (KJV)
description: Psalm 80 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 81 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 110. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 110.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 80. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 81. Greek verse numbers follow the Septuagint, which counts the superscription as verse 1; English verse numbers follow the KJV, so they run 1 behind the Greek. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>ειϲ το τελοϲ ϋπερ των ληνων ψαλμοϲ τω αϲαφʼ <sup>2</sup>αγαλλιαϲθε τω θω τω βοηθω ημων αλαλαξατε τω θω ϊακωβ <sup>3</sup>λαβετε ψαλμον και δοτε τυμπανον ψαλτηριον τερπνον μετα κιθαραϲ <sup>4</sup>ϲαλπιϲατε εν νεομηνια ϲαλπιγγι εν ευϲημω ημερα εορτηϲ ημων <sup>5</sup>οτι προϲταγμα τω ϊϲραηλ εϲτιν και κριμα τω θω ϊακωβ
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob. <sup>2</sup>Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel, the pleasant harp with the psaltery. <sup>3</sup>Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day. <sup>4</sup>For this
was a statute for Israel,
and a law of the God of Jacob.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>μαρτυριον εν τω ϊωϲηφ εθετο αυτον εν τω εξελθεν αυτον εκ γηϲ αιγυπτου γλωϲϲαν ην ουκ εγνω ηκουϲεν <sup>7</sup>απεϲτηϲεν απο αρϲεων τον νωτον αυτου αι χειρεϲ αυτου εν τω κοφινω εδουλευϲαν <sup>8</sup>εν θλιψει επεκαλεϲω μαι και ερυϲαμην ϲε επηκουϲα ϲου εν αποκρυφω καταιγιδοϲ εδοκιμαϲα ϲε επι ϋδατοϲ αντιλογιαϲ διαψαλμα <sup>9</sup>ακουϲον λαοϲ μου και λαληϲω ϲοι ϊϲραηλ και διαμαρτυρομαι ϲοι εαν ακουϲηϲ μου <sup>10</sup>ουκ εϲται εν ϲοι θϲ προϲφατοϲ ουδε προϲκυνηϲειϲ θω αλλοτριω
translation.text:
<sup>5</sup>This he ordained in Joseph
for a testimony, when he went out through the land of Egypt:
where I heard a language
that
 I understood not. <sup>6</sup>I removed his shoulder from the burden: his hands were delivered from the pots. <sup>7</sup>Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder: I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah. <sup>8</sup>Hear, O my people, and I will testify unto thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken unto me; <sup>9</sup>There shall no strange god be in thee; neither shalt thou worship any strange god.

translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>εγω γαρ ειμι κϲ ο θϲ ϲου ο αναγαγων ϲε εκ γηϲ αιγυπτου πλατυνον το ϲτομα ϲου και πληρωϲω αυτο <sup>12</sup>και ουκ ηκουϲεν ο λαοϲ μου τηϲ φωνηϲ μου και ιϲραηλ ου προϲεϲχεν μοι <sup>13</sup>και εξαπεϲτεϲτειλα αυτουϲ κατα τα επιτηδευματα των καρδιων αυτω πορευϲονται εν τοιϲ επιτηδευμαϲιν αυτων <sup>14</sup>ει ο λαοϲ ηκουϲεν μου ϊϲραλ ταιϲ οδοιϲ μου ει επορευθη <sup>15</sup>εν τω μηδενι αν τουϲ εχθρουϲ αυτων εταπινωϲα και επι τουϲ θλιβονταϲ αυτουϲ επεβαλον την χειρα μου
translation.text:
<sup>10</sup>I
am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it. <sup>11</sup>But my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me. <sup>12</sup>So I gave them up unto their own hearts’ lust:
and they walked in their own counsels. <sup>13</sup>Oh that my people had hearkened unto me,
and Israel had walked in my ways! <sup>14</sup>I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries.

translation.original_text: <sup>16</sup>οι εχθροι κυ εψευϲαντο αυτω και εϲται ο καιροϲ αυτων ειϲ τον αιωνα <sup>17</sup>και εψωμιϲεν αυτουϲ εκ ϲτεατοϲ πυρου και εκ πετραϲ μελι εχορταϲεν αυτουϲ
translation.text: <sup>15</sup>The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves unto him: but their time should have endured for ever. <sup>16</sup>He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
